sections.text: Every Rust program starts running at a function called main. Inside it, println! prints a line of text.
A function is a named block of instructions. The curly braces { } mark where it starts and ends. The computer runs the lines inside main from top to bottom.

Coming from another language: println! ends in ! because it's a macro, not a function. Macros are expanded into ordinary code at compile time. That lets println! take any number of arguments and check its format string against them before the program runs.
fn declares a function. Statements end with a semicolon. Strings go in double quotes.
